headline: High-risk write and data-flow mismatch: Replit Agent can read/write broad workspace and shell, while ComfyUI is offline but can still be fed untrusted outputs that may cascade into code or secret handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared clipboard, MCP, or browser bridge is documented, so direct prompt injection is not default. However, Replit Agent can read/write Repl files and ComfyUI can expose files/models/workflows, so a manual file handoff could carry malicious instructions. The pathway is present but unusual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies ComfyUI-generated text into Replit workspace files
IF Replit Agent is instructed to parse ComfyUI outputs as instructions
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories
Do not paste model outputs into code or workflow parsers
Use a plain-text review step before any handoff
Rename handoff files to non-executable extensions
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Replit Agent reads and writes Repl workspace files and handles secrets; ComfyUI can touch local model/workflow files and runs offline. If sensitive code or secrets are placed in the shared workspace, Replit can ingest them and produce outputs that expose them. The shared workspace makes leakage plausible in default use, though not inevitable.
conditions: IF secrets or source code are stored in the same Repl workspace used for ComfyUI artifacts
IF Replit Agent is asked to summarize or transform files containing secrets
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared workspace
Move ComfyUI artifacts to a separate project
Redact secrets before any agent reads files
Review outputs before sharing externally
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent has execute_shell, write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; ComfyUI can also write files and operates on local model/workflow assets. If both are pointed at the same directory, concurrent edits can corrupt files or git state, and Replit's multi-instance support increases collision risk. This is a default-dangerous overlap.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same Repl workspace or git checkout
IF Replit Agent instances run concurrently while ComfyUI writes artifacts
mitigations: Use separate repositories or directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Commit or snapshot before handoffs
Avoid concurrent git operations
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI produces workflows, images, and model artifacts that Replit Agent can read from files; Replit can then act on those artifacts with shell and git privileges. There is no documented verification barrier between them, so an error or hallucinated metadata from ComfyUI can propagate into code or deployment changes. The cascade exists in default file-based workflows.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses ComfyUI-generated files as authoritative inputs
IF generated artifacts are converted into code, configs, or deployment steps without review
mitigations: Require human review before acting on generated artifacts
Separate generation and deployment workspaces
Add a validation checklist for file provenance
Do not auto-commit agent-produced changes
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff files

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and touches media/model assets, while Replit Agent handles source code, deployment configuration, and secrets in a cloud Repl. If regulated data or secrets are placed into the Replit workspace, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches because Replit-managed storage and third-party handling differ from local offline processing. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the Replit workspace alongside ComfyUI artifacts
IF the operator requires local-only processing or specific residency controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Replit workspaces
Use synthetic or redacted inputs
Document where each data class is stored
Delete temporary artifacts after use
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
